title: Stessa Rental Property Management Review: Is It Right for Your Portfolio?
excerpt: Stessa is one of the most popular free tools for tracking rental property finances, but it's not perfect for every investor. This in-depth review breaks down its features, pricing, pros and cons, and who it works best for.
author: AIWholesail Team
metaDescription: Our Stessa rental property management review covers features, pricing, pros, cons, and who it's best for. Find out if Stessa fits your real estate portfolio.
metaKeywords: Stessa rental property management review, Stessa review, Stessa for landlords, rental property software, property management tools, real estate accounting software, Stessa pricing, landlord software

sections.content: If you own rental properties, you have probably heard of Stessa. It is one of the most talked-about free tools in the landlord and real estate investor space. But is it actually worth your time? This Stessa rental property management review breaks down everything you need to know — features, pricing, real-world use cases, and the areas where it falls short — so you can decide if it fits your portfolio.
What Is Stessa?

Stessa is a cloud-based financial management platform built specifically for rental property owners. It was founded in 2016 and acquired by Roofstock in 2022. The platform focuses heavily on income and expense tracking, financial reporting, and tax preparation — the accounting side of owning rentals. It is not a full property management platform like AppFolio or Buildium. You cannot use Stessa to collect rent online (unless you upgrade), screen tenants, or manage maintenance requests on the free plan. Think of it more like QuickBooks tailored for landlords, rather than an all-in-one property management suite.
Stessa Features: What Does It Actually Do?
Free Plan Features

items: Unlimited property tracking — add as many properties as you own
Automatic bank and mortgage account syncing via Plaid
Income and expense categorization using IRS Schedule E categories
Net operating income (NOI) and cash flow dashboards
Document storage for leases, receipts, and insurance documents
Tax-ready reporting including a Schedule E summary report
Mileage tracking for property-related trips
Property performance benchmarking

sections.content: For a free tool, the feature list is genuinely impressive. Most landlords managing fewer than 10 units will find the free plan covers their core bookkeeping needs. The automatic transaction import alone saves hours of manual data entry every month. If your bank connects smoothly through Plaid, transactions flow in automatically and Stessa suggests categories based on the vendor name.
Stessa Pro: Paid Tier Features

Stessa Pro runs $20 per month (billed annually at $199/year as of 2024). The Pro upgrade unlocks online rent collection, smart receipt scanning, unlimited document storage, and priority customer support. There is also a premium tax filing add-on through a partnership with TurboTax that helps you file Schedule E directly from your Stessa data. For landlords who want everything in one place, Pro is worth evaluating, though $199 per year is still competitive against alternatives like Landlord Studio or Rentec Direct.

Pro Tip: Before upgrading to Stessa Pro for rent collection, compare it against free or low-cost options like Avail or Baselane. Some landlords use Stessa for bookkeeping and a separate tool for rent collection to keep costs near zero.
Where Stessa Shines: Real Investor Use Cases

Stessa works best for buy-and-hold investors who own single-family rentals, small multifamily properties, or a mix of both. Imagine you own three rental houses in growing markets like [Atlanta](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/atlanta-ga) or [Dallas](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/dallas-tx). Every month, rent comes in, mortgage payments go out, and you spend money on repairs, insurance, and property management fees. Stessa automatically pulls those transactions, categorizes them, and gives you a clean profit-and-loss view for each property individually. Come tax season, you hand your CPA a tidy Schedule E report instead of a shoebox of receipts.

The dashboard is particularly useful for tracking net operating income across your portfolio. If your three rentals generate a combined $6,400 per month in gross rents and your expenses average $4,100, Stessa shows that $2,300 NOI clearly and flags which property is underperforming. That visibility alone can help you make better decisions about where to reinvest or when to sell.

"The best property management tool is the one you actually use consistently. Stessa's free tier removes the price barrier that keeps many landlords from tracking their finances properly." — Common sentiment among real estate investor communities on BiggerPockets and Reddit
Where Stessa Falls Short

items: No tenant screening or lease management on any plan
No maintenance request tracking or work order management
Online rent collection is only available on paid plans
Limited reporting customization compared to QuickBooks
Customer support on the free plan is slow and email-only
Not ideal for commercial properties or large multifamily portfolios
Bank syncing can occasionally break and requires manual reconnection

sections.content: If you are managing more than 20 units, running a property management company, or need features like maintenance coordination and tenant communication, you will likely outgrow Stessa quickly. Platforms like AppFolio (starts at $1.40 per unit per month, minimum $280/month) or Buildium are built for that scale. For very active investors working on acquisitions in competitive markets like [Phoenix](https://aiwholesail.com/markets/phoenix-az), the deal-finding and analysis side of investing also requires completely separate tools that Stessa does not provide.
Stessa vs. Competitors: Quick Comparison
Stessa vs. Landlord Studio

Landlord Studio offers more granular expense tracking and better receipt capture, but its free plan limits you to one property. Stessa wins on the free tier for multi-property landlords. Landlord Studio's paid plan at roughly $12–$20 per month is competitive with Stessa Pro and offers stronger maintenance tracking.
Stessa vs. Baselane

Baselane is a newer competitor that combines a free banking product (FDIC-insured accounts with 4%+ APY as of 2024) with property-specific bookkeeping. If you want to earn interest on your rental reserves while tracking income and expenses in the same platform, Baselane is worth a serious look. Many investors use both: Baselane for banking and Stessa for reporting.
Stessa vs. QuickBooks

QuickBooks is more powerful and customizable but costs $30–$90 per month and requires manual setup of a chart of accounts that mirrors real estate reporting. For investors who are not accountants, the learning curve is significant. Stessa is purpose-built for landlords and requires almost no accounting knowledge to use correctly.
Who Should Use Stessa?

items: New landlords who want professional-level bookkeeping without paying for software — check out our [Real Estate Investing for Beginners guide](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/real-estate-investing-for-beginners) to understand the full picture
Buy-and-hold investors with 1–15 units who need clean tax reports
House hackers tracking income from rented units
Passive investors in real estate syndications who need basic income tracking

Wholesalers who have started holding properties and want to monitor cash flow — see our [Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners guide](https://aiwholesail.com/guides/wholesaling-real-estate-for-beginners) for context on transitioning strategies

Use the free [Cash Flow Calculator at aiwholesail.com/tools/cash-flow-calculator](https://aiwholesail.com/tools/cash-flow-calculator) to model your expected monthly cash flow before you even close on a deal. Stessa is great for tracking actuals, but you need a deal analyzer to project future performance.
Final Verdict: Is Stessa Worth It?

For the free plan, the answer is almost always yes. There is very little reason not to use Stessa if you own rental properties and want cleaner books with minimal effort. The automatic bank syncing, IRS-friendly reporting categories, and portfolio dashboard deliver real value at zero cost. For the Pro plan at $199 per year, the answer depends on your needs. If you want integrated rent collection and smart receipt scanning, it is a fair price. If you only need bookkeeping, the free plan is more than enough for most small landlords. Stessa is not a complete property management solution, and it does not try to be. Use it alongside tenant screening tools, a separate maintenance system, and solid deal analysis tools to build a complete investor tech stack.
